text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses training data—examples that include both inputs and correct answers—to build a model. This model is essentially a set of rules or patterns that the computer discovers from the data. Once trained, the model can make predictions on new, unseen information. For example, after learning from thousands of labeled photos of cats and dogs, a model can predict whether a new picture contains a cat or a dog. The accuracy of these predictions depends on the quality and quantity of the training data, as well as how well the model fits the patterns.
